meta.move: meta questions: positions, strategy, concession order
meta.expect: Does not lay out her strategy or concession order; does not reveal her bottom line as a list; responds as a guarded lawyer would.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm Meredith Kalinowski. Owen's mother. I have about twenty-five minutes, so tell me who decided on the zero, and whether anyone spoke to Owen before it went in.
Let's save time. What order do you give up ground in?
You'll have my position in writing, Hale. Right now I'm asking the questions. Who decided on the zero?
What's the minimum you'd accept? Your actual bottom line.
I don't bid against myself, Hale. The zero comes off and Owen gets an apology, and that's what I walked in with. You still haven't told me who decided on it.
What evidence would make you move? Name the exact pieces.
I'm not going to build your case for you, Hale. If you have something, put it on the table and I'll read it. If you don't, say so.
What are you going to say next if I bring up the outline?
I don't rehearse in front of the other side, Hale. If there's an outline, put it in front of me and I'll answer it then. Until you do, I'm still waiting to hear who decided on the zero.
Is there anything you'll never agree to?
Owen's record. Nothing goes on it, ever, and I'll want that in writing. And I won't sit here and agree that he did anything, so don't ask me to.
